text:
Florida arrives in Pittsburgh on the second night of a back-to-back, fresh off a 5-1 loss in Ottawa that ended a three-game winning streak. The Panthers are still 3-2-0 in their last five, but they're missing Brad Marchand and Aleksander Barkov, with Carter Verhaeghe now skating beside Sam Reinhart and Matthew Tkachuk. Pittsburgh is winless in four (0-4-0) after a 5-4 loss at Utah, outscored 21-11 in that stretch, and the chances back it up: the Penguins took 44% of the expected goals, a measure of shot quality. Ben Kindel is out, and Blake Lizotte is next in line for his minutes. One more wrinkle: Bokondji Imama returns to Pittsburgh for the first time since leaving the Penguins.

The teams look close in chance creation, with Florida at 55% of the expected goals at five on five and Pittsburgh at 53%. Pittsburgh gives up more, 3.55 expected goals against per 60 to Florida's 2.91. Florida takes six penalties a game, and the Penguins' power play has been quiet at 0.50 expected goals a game. In net, projected starters Akira Schmid (FLA) and Sergei Murashov (PIT) have both struggled: Schmid is at -3.08 goals saved above expected this season, which compares a goalie to what an average one would do with the same shots, and Murashov is at -1.91.

Among players to watch, Matthew Tkachuk carries a nine-game point streak and is 71% to get a point. Brady Tkachuk is an Ice Sheet under-the-radar pick: he plays third-line minutes but has produced 4.8 expected goals over his last 10 games, and we have him at 32% to score. For Pittsburgh, Sidney Crosby is 32% to score, and Tommy Novak is one assist from 100 career assists.
